name: Weeze (Niederrhein) Airport
before:
A small Ryanair airport in the Lower Rhine region of Germany, 3.7 km south west of the town of Weeze.

The marketing name is a trap. It is sometimes sold as Düsseldorf-Weeze, but Düsseldorf is a long way off: the airport is 48 km north west of Duisburg and 33 km south east of Nijmegen in the Netherlands. Direct buses to Düsseldorf main station run up to seven times a day and take an hour and a quarter. Quote that transfer explicitly, because a client booking Düsseldorf will not expect it.

There is no rail station at the airport. Shuttle buses run to Weeze, Kevelaer and Goch stations, and local buses serve Kleve, Emmerich, Goch, Geldern and Nijmegen.

One terminal with nine stands for aircraft up to a 737-800. There are no jet bridges, because the apron is to the west of the terminal rather than in front of it, so six stands are bus-boarded and only three can be walked to.
after:
A small Ryanair airport in the Lower Rhine region of Germany, just south west of the town of Weeze. It handled more than 2.2 million passengers in 2025, up 14 per cent on 2024.

The marketing name is a trap. Ryanair sells it as Düsseldorf Weeze, but the airport is more than 60 km from Düsseldorf: it is 48 km north west of Duisburg and 33 km south east of Nijmegen in the Netherlands. Direct coaches to Düsseldorf's central bus station, by the main station, take an hour and a quarter and run several times a day. Quote that transfer explicitly, because a client booking Düsseldorf will not expect it.

There is no railway station at the airport. Buses link it with the stations at Weeze, Kevelaer and Goch. One line runs on to Nijmegen.

The municipality of Weeze puts the airfield site 2 km south west of the village centre and Wikipedia puts the airport 3.7 km south west, so the direction is agreed but the figure is not; Weeze is too small for the GeoNames check. The operator puts Weeze station 5 minutes away by car.

claims.claim: more than 2.2 million passengers in 2025
claims.inAfter: It handled more than 2.2 million passengers in 2025
claims.note: The old text gave no figure; added as the current measure behind "small". ADV 2,245,473 and Eurostat 2,245,090; the airport marked its 2 millionth passenger of 2025 in December 2025 and expects about 2.25 million in 2026.

claims.claim: up 14 per cent on 2024
claims.note: ADV gives 14.0 per cent; Eurostat's figures give 14.0 per cent (1,970,158 to 2,245,090).

claims.claim: Ryanair sells it as Düsseldorf Weeze
claims.inAfter: Ryanair sells it as Düsseldorf Weeze
claims.note: Was "It is sometimes sold as Düsseldorf-Weeze". Ryanair's own airport data names it Dusseldorf Weeze and files it under its Düsseldorf city code. Current Wikipedia adds that a court blocked the Düsseldorf name in 2016 as likely to mislead; not in the text, as it has only one source here.

sources.quote: However, Ryanair still refers to it as "Düsseldorf-Weeze".

claims.claim: more than 60 km from Düsseldorf
claims.inAfter: the airport is more than 60 km from Düsseldorf
claims.note: Replaces "Düsseldorf is a long way off" with a figure both sources support: the coordinates give 61.0 km in a straight line from the centre of Düsseldorf, and Wikipedia gives 83 km, presumably by road (a ratio of 1.36, inside the 0.8 to 1.6 allowed). The operator itself places Düsseldorf within an 80 km radius.

claims.claim: 3.7 km south west of Weeze
claims.wasBefore: 3.7 km south west of the town of Weeze
claims.why: Sources disagree on the figure (Wikipedia 3.7 km, the municipality 2 km from the village centre) and Weeze is too small for the GeoNames check. Softened to "just south west".

claims.claim: Düsseldorf is a long way off
claims.wasBefore: but Düsseldorf is a long way off
claims.why: Replaced by the distance both sources support: more than 60 km.

claims.claim: up to seven times a day
claims.wasBefore: run up to seven times a day
claims.why: The 2026 timetable has at most six a day each way; Wikipedia says seven. Softened to several times a day.

claims.claim: direct buses to Düsseldorf main station
claims.wasBefore: Direct buses to Düsseldorf main station
claims.why: The coach stops at the central bus station beside the main station; corrected in the text.

claims.claim: local buses to Kleve, Emmerich and Geldern
claims.wasBefore: local buses serve Kleve, Emmerich, Goch, Geldern and Nijmegen
claims.why: Only Wikipedia names Kleve, Emmerich and Geldern; the operator's bus page lists SB46 (Kevelaer, Weeze, Goch, Nijmegen) and its timetables do not reach those towns. Goch and Nijmegen are kept.

claims.claim: one terminal with nine stands for aircraft up to a 737-800
claims.wasBefore: One terminal with nine stands for aircraft up to a 737-800.
claims.why: Only Wikipedia. The operator's facts page does not give it and the German AIP shows stands only as chart images. The operator broke ground on 14 August 2026 on a new arrivals terminal, due in mid-2027 with separate Schengen and non-Schengen halls, but that has only the operator's own page (the builder's site, goldbeck.de, answered 429), so it is not in the text either.

claims.claim: no jet bridges; six stands bus-boarded, three walked to
claims.wasBefore: There are no jet bridges, because the apron is to the west of the terminal rather than in front of it, so six stands are bus-boarded and only three can be walked to.
claims.why: Only Wikipedia; no second source found.

opinion.text: The marketing name is a trap.
opinion.why: Framing kept from the original. The facts behind it, the Düsseldorf Weeze name and the distance, follow with two sources each.

opinion.text: Quote that transfer explicitly, because a client booking Düsseldorf will not expect it.
